notes: runtime-audit-results.json is the final clean-source full matrix against 2620a6a, five rounds with 21 repetitions (105 samples per series).
The live-heap experiment isolates removal of propertyNames after 25e96d0; it was measured with those two source-file deletions uncommitted, then retained by 4c695ff.

The collectibility audit and initial regression follow-up were measured at 2620a6a before this pass. The final factory cleanup keeps the same tracked-template path and removes optional-state branching.
Rejected experiments are dirty-source measurements at 4c695ff. No snapshot or signal production shortcut was retained.

One-off memory and profile scripts were /tmp/framekit-memory.mjs, /tmp/framekit-live-heap.mjs, and /tmp/framekit-investigate.mjs. Their results are diagnostics, not CI assertions or maintained entry points.

Traces and CPU profiles remain locally under /tmp/framekit-audit-profiles. GC overlap unions complete main-thread V8.GC/MinorGC/MajorGC intervals, clipping to operation windows; nested events are not double-counted.
Every CPU capture had non-monotonic time deltas, so weighted CPU percentages and operation sample attribution are omitted. Trace windows remain separate from uninstrumented timing runs.

collectibility.methodology: 50 detached documents × 10 semantic Frame tags, then ten mounted 1,000-row lifetimes with layout, native hover and property observers. Destroyed nodes referenced only via WeakRef. Two explicit full GC requests after each phase, outside page JS jobs. DOM counters include bounded per-document templates. No retained-heap size assertion.

liveTreeHeap.methodology: Seven fresh-page pairs with alternating version order. 5,000 default Frames plus parent/ScreenGui mounted alive. Full GC twice before each heap reading, outside page JS jobs. Runtime.getHeapUsage usedSize delta from pre-tree baseline; includes JS wrapper and framework costs, not total process/native memory.
